Choose the scenarios of a run

Source: R/scenarios.R
scenarios.Rd

scenarios() checks the scenario table cfg$scenarios and returns it, or the rows of the scenarios in only. The real data is the scenario "real", and each other scenario is fake.

Usage

scenarios(cfg, only = NULL)

Arguments

cfg

The config list of the project, normally CFG from <version>_functions/_cfg.R. It MUST have the element scenarios.

only

NULL for every scenario, or a character vector of scenario names.

Value

A data.frame with the columns scenario, sims, output when cfg$scenarios has it, and each setting column. It has one row for each chosen scenario in the order of cfg$scenarios. sims is an integer.

Details

cfg$scenarios MUST be a data.frame with these columns:

  • scenario: unique names that match ^[a-z0-9_]+$. One name MUST be "real".

  • sims: the number of simulations of the scenario, a whole number of 1 or more.

  • output: optional. TRUE or FALSE on each row, and FALSE for "real". make_outputs() writes the output of a fake scenario with TRUE. This column is not a setting. It is not in the argsets, in the key of the cache or in manifest$settings.

Each other column is a setting of the scenario, for example n_boot for a number of bootstrap replicates that is smaller in the fake scenarios. A setting column MUST be an atomic vector, and its name MUST be syntactic. It MUST have a value for each fake scenario. It MAY have NA for "real", when only the fake scenarios use the setting. The argsets of "real", its cache key and its manifest$settings then do not hold the setting. A data function MUST NOT take such a setting as an argument: plnr finds no value of it for "real", and run_plan() stops. Its name MUST NOT be one of scenario, sim, analysis, seed, index_analysis, name, fn, fn_name, data and argset. add_analyses() puts the setting of the scenario into each argset.

scenarios() stops on a table that breaks a rule, and on a name in only that is not in the table. The error names the problem.

pbn keeps the value of the last call of scenarios() in this R session, and initialize_project() removes it. add_data() gives it to the plan, and get_data() reads it there before add_analyses().

See also

vignette("pbn"), which builds and runs a small fake project.

Other project setup: create_project(), end_unless_real(), folder(), initialize_project(), new_version()

Examples

CFG <- list(
  scenarios = data.frame(
    scenario = c("real", "null"),
    sims = c(1, 3),
    n_boot = c(200, 20)
  )
)
pbn::scenarios(CFG)
#>   scenario sims n_boot
#> 1     real    1    200
#> 2     null    3     20
pbn::scenarios(CFG, only = "null")
#>   scenario sims n_boot
#> 1     null    3     20
